<Rep. John B. Larson>: Thank you, Mr. Neal. And thank you, Mr. Chairman. And let me commend Mr. Smucker as well. The premise of the Social Security Child Protection Act is a good one. I think I, and everyone on this committee, wants to protect children from identity theft, as I'm sure everyone on this committee agrees. No one should have their identity or financial well-being jeopardized by bad actors.
Social Security is the number one anti-poverty program for the elderly, and it's also the number one anti-poverty program for children, until, of course, we renew the expanded child tax credit. Social Security alone lifts more than 900,000 children out of poverty. And yet, Congress hasn't enhanced it in more than 54 years.
If this was really about protecting children's social security benefits, we would be discussing our plan to protect social security from Trump's privatization scheme. And we would be expanding benefits, not handing them over to an unvetted, unaccountable, so-called DOGE. Since President Trump took office, 7,000 staff have been cut from Social Security. Is there even going to be anyone left to issue these numbers to children who have been impacted? Or will it be outsourced to AI chatbots?
And what about DOGE's meddling with data at Social Security? While I support the effort this bill is attempting to make, and was proud to support it before, I cannot vote for it in the current form, knowing that it does nothing to address the data being put at risk at Social Security as we speak. We need answers and accountability from DOGE and Social Security. They may say that everything is safe and secure for now, but I want to have them come before this committee and tell me under oath. I would think that everyone on this committee would want that. We cannot afford to play it safe.
The American people deserve to see their elected officials taking action and asking all the tough questions and protecting their benefits and information from abuse. I've been sounding the alarm on this issue for months and introduced a bill in March blocking DOGE from accessing Americans' data at Social Security.
That's why I'm introducing it as an amendment. I implore all of my colleagues to join me in this effort to block DOGE from accessing their constituents' information.
Sincerely,
John B. Larson.
